summary:
Space Time Capsule is an immersive, 3D web-based museum designed to tell the stories of NASA hardware left on the Moon, Mars, and deep space. Addressing the challenge, we transformed dense historical data into an engaging narrative for school-age space enthusiasts. Users can inspect detailed 3D models of the Apollo Lunar Module, Voyager probes, and Mars rovers to understand the engineering behind their discoveries.

To make the science tangible, we developed interactive "Digital Twin" laboratories. Players can simulate deep-space power budgets, plan autonomous rover traverses, and explore lunar polar prospecting. The platform also features an interactive Apollo landing-site map and evidence-based forensics that teach users to distinguish between verified data and educational reconstructions.

Built entirely with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, the app runs directly in any modern browser without a backend. By combining real NASA data, 3D visualization, and interactive simulation, it creates a narrative-driven experience that inspires the next generation of explorers and honors the silent monuments of space exploration.
details:
Project Title: Space Time Capsule: Interactive Space Heritage & Digital Twin Museum

Overview:
Space Time Capsule is a comprehensive, browser-based interactive museum and engineering simulation platform that brings the untold stories of NASA’s legacy hardware to life. Addressing the challenge of making historical space artifacts engaging for school-age enthusiasts and the public, we developed a rich, 3D-driven web experience. The project highlights equipment left on the Moon, Mars, and deep space—ranging from Apollo Lunar Modules and rovers to the Voyager probes—teaching users not only what these machines are, but how they operate and the scientific discoveries they enabled.

Core Features and Interactive Modules:

1. The Glass Spacecraft Museum & 3D Model Lab:
At the heart of the experience is an interactive gallery featuring official NASA 3D GLB models. Users can drag, rotate, and inspect detailed engineering models of the Apollo Lunar Module, Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV), Viking Lander, InSight, Opportunity, Curiosity, Perseverance, and the Voyager probes. Each exhibit is paired with mission timelines, engineering specifications, and verified archival evidence.
2. Interactive Lunar Evidence Map & Moon Trek Integration:
We built an evidence-aware map of Apollo landing sites, distinguishing between confirmed historical coordinates and uncertain artifacts. This is coupled with an embedded live view of NASA's Moon Trek tool, allowing users to explore real lunar topography.
3. Advanced Digital Twins & Engineering Labs:
· Deep Space Systems Engineering Lab: Users operate a Voyager digital twin, managing Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (RTG) power constraints, calculating one-way light-time delays, and exploring idealized X-band link budgets.
· Autonomous Planetary Rover Science Lab: A terrain-based planner where users input traverse distance, slope, and hazard density. The system calculates risk indices and generates a simulated autonomous route for rovers like Perseverance.
· Procedural 3D Surface Labs: Utilizing Three.js, we created real-time 3D environments for the Apollo LRV and the VIPER lunar rover, allowing users to replay traverses, deploy drills, and analyze polar terrain risks.
4. Frontier X Modules (Advanced Autonomy & AI Simulation):
· Mission Command & AI Autonomy Center: A deterministic, rule-based simulation where users manage spacecraft telemetry, respond to fault injections (thermal, power, comms), and compare human decisions against an AI policy.
· Autonomous Multi-Robot Exploration: A grid-based simulation demonstrating cooperative A* pathfinding. Users command a swarm of four robots, inject failures, and watch the remaining units reassign tasks and replan routes.
· Evidence & Reproducibility Tracker: Users can record their simulation parameters, extract JSON evidence packages, and track their scientific reasoning locally.
5. Scientific Forensics & Story Engine:
To teach scientific literacy, the "Evidence Forensics Lab" challenges users to evaluate claims (e.g., "Are ALSEP experiments still running?"). The app explicitly distinguishes between primary NASA data, verified historical facts, and educational reconstructions. A narrative Story Engine guides users through the transition from landing to legacy.

Technical Implementation & Data Integrity:
The application is built entirely with vanilla HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, requiring no backend, database, or build tools. It utilizes the Google <model-viewer> web component for NASA 3D assets and Three.js for procedural 3D environments. Live data is pulled from the NASA Image and Video Library API (keyless) for archival galleries.

Scientific integrity is our highest priority. Every simulation explicitly labels generated telemetry as "educational heuristics" or "synthetic data." We do not claim live access to spacecraft telemetry. Users are consistently reminded of the difference between a NASA-verified engineering model and a real-time mission feed.

Educational Impact:
By merging real NASA data, 3D visualization, and interactive simulation, Space Time Capsule transforms passive reading into active investigation. It inspires the next generation of explorers by giving them the tools to think like mission controllers, planetary geologists, and aerospace engineers.
